newsitem.title: JAPAN: Britain's Clarke sees sustained economic growth.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Clarke sees sustained economic growth.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday that the British economy has every prospect of sustained growth.

Asked by reporters during a visit to Japan to comment on Prime Minister John Major's remarks that the strength of the pound has hurt British export competitiveness, Clarke said: "I know the prime minister did say that. We have a floating exchange rate, we don't have a target exchange rate. It has strengthened a bit but the British economy has never been better. We have every prospect of sustained growth."
Emerging from a meeting with Japanese Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso, he told reporters Japan's deregulation and reforms are the key for improving the Japanese economy.
"Reforms and deregulation, in my opinion, must be the key to improve Japan's economic performance," he said.
Clarke said Aso explained Japan's plans to deregulate and reform its financial markets.
"I'm particularly interested in prospects for reform in the financial markets here," he said.
Clarke arrived in Japan on Wednesday to meet senior Japanese government officials.
